There are SEVEN fixes here. They share one build and one checker, which is why they are one task.
Do them in this order; each has its own required negative control.

=== FIX 1 (BLOCKER A1) -- the Unparsed fallback does not exist ===

briefs/M1-plan.md 4.5 specifies a final fallback rule: "a line no rule consumes -> Unparsed --
must be zero corpus-wide", and 8.2 calls zero-Unparsed "the strongest single parser check", with
8.4 requiring a negative control that introduces an unclassifiable line. NONE of that is real:
Types.hs:47 declares the constructor, but Markdown.hs never constructs it -- the final branch of
parseBlocksEngine always builds Para. Consequently Stats.hs:80 hard-codes stUnparsed = 0,
CheckContent's golden check merely compares that literal against 0, and group 3 searches the model
for a constructor the producer cannot emit. All three advertised gates are incapable of ever
being red, and 8.4's negative control cannot be performed as written.

Codex's reachability qualification is correct and you must respect it: at HEAD nothing can hang,
because isParaLine (Markdown.hs:394-400) is exactly the conjunction of the six preceding guards'
negations, so span always consumes at least the current line. The hazard is a ONE-SIDED future
edit: add a block rule to isParaLine's exclusions without a consuming guard (or the reverse) and
span returns ([], sameInput), a Para [] is prepended, and go recurses on an identical list
forever. The Opus reviewer demonstrated this with a partial revert: content-check ran >10 minutes
without terminating instead of failing.

Do all four of these:
  1a. Make the final branch progress-safe UNCONDITIONALLY: if span consumes no line, emit
      Unparsed l and recurse on ls. Termination must then hold for every finite input regardless
      of predicate drift.
  1b. Remove the drift hazard at its root: derive the guard chain and isParaLine from a SINGLE
      exported line classifier, so the two can no longer disagree. 1a makes drift survivable;
      1b makes it unlikely. Do both.
  1c. Make the fallback provably REACHABLE. This is the hard part and the reason 8.4 was never
      demonstrable: in this grammar the paragraph rule is a genuine catch-all, so no corpus line
      can reach the fallback. Expose a test seam -- e.g. a classifier-injecting variant of the
      engine, with production passing the real classifier -- so a fixture can feed a line the
      classifier declines. The fixture MUST construct a real Unparsed block, assert it is
      produced, and assert the engine terminates on that input. An unreachable branch is not a
      fallback; it is dead code with a comment.
  1d. Stop stUnparsed being a literal WITHOUT breaking the 4.4 laziness contract. The browser must
      not start forcing all 108 pages' blocks at boot. Required shape: the stats JSON schema does
      NOT change; the content-check producer computes 'unparsed' from the parsed model, while the
      app keeps the cheap raw-scan value, documented as such. A real Unparsed then makes
      content-check --json disagree with the DOM and the existing three-way agreement turns it
      red. Group 3 keeps asserting zero over the real corpus and is now meaningful because the
      producer can finally emit.
  1e. CORRECT THE PROSE. The false claim is codified in three places and will re-mislead the next
      reviewer: Stats.hs:74-79 ("exe:content-check ... that is the actual gate"), CheckContent.hs's
      group-3 header comment, and -- report this, do not edit it, you do not own briefs/ --
      briefs/M1-plan.md 4.5/8.2/8.4. Rewrite the two comments you own to state what is actually
      guaranteed: structural progress, a reachable-by-fixture fallback, and a model-derived count
      in the checker only.
  NEGATIVE CONTROL 1: the fixture of 1c must be shown producing Unparsed (paste it). Additionally,
  reintroduce a one-sided classifier edit, confirm the parse now TERMINATES and reports Unparsed
  instead of hanging, and restore. That second control is the whole point of 1a.

=== FIX 2 (BLOCKER NEW1) -- the outline misattributes subsections and breaks breadcrumbs ===

Outline.hs:54-77 keeps only (page, level, text) -- within-page order is discarded. attachSubs
(95-101) ends each section at nextSectionPage - 1, so when two section-level headings share a
page the earlier one gets secEndPage < secPage, owns no page at all, and every same-page
subsection falls into the LATER section. Reproduced in the built app:

  Startup Guide TOC:  "Try applying an effect" (p.10) shows ZERO subsections, while
                      "Try sampling" (p.10) wrongly owns "Applying an effect" and
                      "How to use the FX1/FX2 buttons".
  Breadcrumbs:        startup-guide p.10 reads ".../ Try sampling /"   (page opens with "Try applying an effect")
                      startup-guide p.14 reads ".../ Trademarks /"     (page opens with "Operating precautions")

Pages with more than one section-level heading: startup-guide 1, 2, 3, 4, 10, 14; midi 2
("2. Product information" + "3. MIDI implementation chart"); oss 11 ("MIT" + "MICROSOFT AZURE
RTOS"). guide-book has NONE, which is why every guide-book golden stayed green.

Fix: carry a monotonic source-order index on each heading event and attach each subsection to the
last SECTION EVENT preceding it in source order, not to a page range. Set secEndPage to the next
section's page minus one only when that next section is on a LATER page, otherwise to this
section's own page -- making secEndPage >= secPage an invariant rather than an accident.

ownership -- startup-guide p.10 "Try applying an effect" owns "Applying an effect" and "How to use
the FX1/FX2 buttons" while "Try sampling" owns "Sampling", plus p.14, midi p.2 and oss p.11;
(c) the golden totals are UNMOVED (sections 29/21/6/5, subsections 78/27/1/0) -- the current bug
preserves totals while corrupting ownership, so a count-only assertion is exactly what missed it.
  NEGATIVE CONTROL 2: restore the nextSectionPage-1 attachment, confirm the new ownership
  assertions fail while the count goldens stay green (this proves the counts never could have
  caught it), then restore.

Every DocStats field is raw-derived: chars/lines/pages are Text ops on raw source,

dedupeSlugs (Markdown.hs:254-261) counts occurrences per ORIGINAL BASE and never reserves what it

assertions would pass while every shared deep link opened at Home.

already ends in '#/m/guide-book/p/17/ja'. Wait for boot and for image decode independently rather
than inheriting the previous target's state, and assert all of: the hash, #page-17, the
'ja-visible' class on #sxc1-page, #ja-panel present, #ja-image src ending
'pages/guide-book/page-17.webp', and a real decode. Keep the existing warm toggle assertions too;

really decoded -- await img.decode() (or complete && naturalWidth > 0) against the EXPECTED src for
that slug and page, with network/resource failure listeners armed so a failed fetch is reported
rather than silently timing out. Chrome is already a hard requirement of this script, so this is
